free_tier.stated: TaskBot Challenge: each selected Entrant Team is eligible for a restricted research grant of $250,000 U.S. paid to its university, intended to support two full-time students or the equivalent and one month of the Faculty Advisor’s salary. Each member and the Faculty Advisor also receive Alexa-enabled devices (at most four per team), free AWS services to support their TaskBot (subject to reasonable limits set by Sponsor) and support from the Alexa team. Overall prizes are separate: $500,000 first place, $100,000 second and $50,000 third. Entry is restricted to students enrolled full-time at an accredited college or university, entering as a team of students from a single University.
free_tier.notes: The $250,000 research grant is paid to each selected university, not to an Entrant Team or any individual entrant, and the university must sign the sponsor's agreements, including IRS forms W-9 or W-8, before the team can take part.

notes: The clearest institutional gate, and the one most likely to be mistaken for open: the public-facing pages describe prizes and cloud support without stating the enrolment rule, which lives in the rules document. The cloud term could mean free AWS for the duration of the challenge, a fixed credit, or standard free-tier limits. The pages say 'free Amazon Web Services ... to support their research and development efforts' and never put a number on it, so the value of the compute is unverified and only the grant is quantified. The route that would price it is the participant agreement, which is not public.
